Trishuli Flow Routing

Terrain flow model · Trishuli–Narayani

Modelled Flood Flow Direction Based on Terrain

Flow-direction and routing model for the 26 August 2026 Trishuli glacial-lake outburst. It traces the flood 305 km from the Nepal–China border to the Indian border and ends 470 m from the known outlet.

Scope

READ FIRST

This flood does not reach Varanasi

The Trishuli becomes the Narayani, enters India as the Gandak and joins the Ganga near Patna, about 230 km downstream of Varanasi. Varanasi's flooding comes from the upper Ganga, Yamuna and Son.

This is a Nepal-only model: the elevation data ends at 27° N and Varanasi is at 25.32° N.

The model uses terrain only. It shows where water flows and where it can spread. Without a breach hydrograph it cannot give exact depth, velocity or arrival time (see Model Limitations below).

The 2D spread map and 3D terrain view animate the flood along this route, with the uncertain parameters as sliders.

How the model works

WORKFLOW

The route

D8 FLOW DIRECTION

Each 60 m cell drains to the steepest of its eight downhill neighbours. Following these steps from the release point gives the route; counting the cells that drain through each point gives the river network.

The route is 305 km long, drops 1 851 m (mean slope 0.61%) and ends 470 m from Triveni, where the Narayani leaves Nepal. This confirms the routing.

Exposure in the corridor

EXPOSURE

All features within 10 m of height above the river they drain to (HAND, Height Above Nearest Drainage), with their height above drainage, distance to the route and distance downstream from the release. Districts are assigned by location, since the hydropower layer's district field is empty for 97% of rows.

Model Limitations

  • No spill-over into other valleys: flood water stays within the main river's drainage area.
  • Flood depth is set by the user: not calculated, as no river flow data is available.

What is needed to predict how deep, how fast and when

Most important first:

  • Lake water discharge time and peak outflow volume
  • River gauge water level records
  • Depth of each riverbed
  • Ground roughness at pixel level

Sources

DATA
  • Elevation: SRTM v3, 1 arc-second tiles, resampled to 60 m.
  • River map data: OpenStreetMap river and canal lines, used for stream burning.
  • Flood start point: Trishuli flood start point as reported by UNOSAT.
  • Observed flood extent: Sentinel-1 flood mask, used only for scoring.
  • Exposure: OpenStreetMap buildings, roads and bridges; hydropower asset layer; district boundaries.
  • Imagery: PlanetScope pre- and post-event pair.

D8 routing on SRTM v3, resampled to 60 m in UTM 45N over 83.60–86.00° E, 27.15–29.00° N (13.9 million cells). Channel network 9 149 km. Built with pysheds, rasterio and geopandas. Sentinel-1 extent used for scoring only.
